To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the age-related decline in total PDE in dystrophic mouse muscle is isozyme specific and not due to decreased PDE activity in general, and that the age-related loss of sensitivity to PDE inhibitors in dystrophic mouse tissue is isozyme-specific.
age-related alterations in cyclic phosphodiesterase in the dystrophic mouse leg muscles are isozyme specific and not due to generalized decrease in total phosphodiesterase.

(a) total PDE activity declines with age in dystrophic muscle; (b) cAMP and cAMP PDE are elevated in dystrophic muscle of young mice; (c) cGMP PDA is not altered in dystrophic muscle at any age; and (d) the sensitivity of PDE to inhibition by RO 20-17 24 and EHNA declines with age in both dystrophic and control muscle

the role of cyclic nucleotides and their metabolism by phosphodiesterases (PDEs) in the regulation of muscle function and metabolism.
the role of cyclic nucleotide phosphoesterases (PDE) and their inhibitors in the pathogenesis of muscular dystrophy.
the role of cyclic nucleotides in muscle development and disease.
